sanskrit: nirindriyo 'bhimanyeta vraṇavān asmi nirvraṇaḥ aliṅgo liṅgam ātmānam akālaḥ kālam ātmanaḥ
english: Though devoid of the senses, he imagines, "I am wounded," though he is woundless; though without attribute, he conceives the marked self as his own, and the self that is beyond time he takes for one bound by time.

sanskrit: asattvaṃ sattvam ātmānam atattvaṃ tattvam ātmanaḥ amṛtyur mṛtyum ātmānam acaraś caram ātmanaḥ
english: The unreal he takes for the real self, the untrue for the true; deathless, he conceives the self as subject to death; unmoving, he takes the self to be in motion.

sanskrit: akṣetraḥ kṣetram ātmānam asargaḥ sargam ātmanaḥ atapās tapa ātmānam agatir gatim ātmanaḥ
english: Fieldless, he takes the field to be the self; uncreated, he conceives himself as created; though beyond austerity, he thinks the self performs austerities; though without going, he imagines the self to have a course.

sanskrit: abhavo bhavam ātmānam abhayo bhayam ātmanaḥ akṣaraḥ kṣaram ātmānam abuddhis tv abhimanyate
english: Free of becoming, he takes the self as caught in becoming; free of fear, as fearful; imperishable, he conceives the self as perishable — thus, lacking awakened insight, he misconceives.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca evam apratibuddhatvād abuddhajanasevanāt sargakoṭisahasrāṇi patanāntāni gacchati
english: Vasiṣṭha said: Thus, through being unawakened and through keeping company with the unawakened, he passes through thousands of millions of creations, each ending in a fall.

sanskrit: dhāmnā dhāmasahasrāṇi maraṇāntāni gacchati tiryagyonau manuṣyatve devaloke tathaiva ca
english: From abode to abode he passes through thousands of dwellings, each ending in death — in the wombs of beasts, in the human state, and likewise in the world of the gods.

sanskrit: candramā iva kośānāṃ punas tatra sahasraśaḥ līyate 'pratibuddhatvād evam eṣa hy abuddhimān
english: As the moon dissolves within its sheaths, so this man, lacking insight, dissolves there again and again by the thousand, all through being unawakened.

sanskrit: kalāḥ pañcadaśā yonis tad dhāma iti paṭhyate nityam etad vijānīhi somaḥ ṣoḍaśamī kalā
english: The womb is the fifteen digits, and that, it is taught, is the abode; know this for certain — the moon is the sixteenth digit.

sanskrit: kalāyāṃ jāyate 'jasraṃ punaḥ punar abuddhimān dhāma tasyopayuñjanti bhūya eva tu jāyate
english: In the digit the man without insight is born ceaselessly, again and again; they consume his dwelling, and yet once more he is born.

sanskrit: ṣoḍaśī tu kalā sūkṣmā sa soma upadhāryatām na tūpayujyate devair devān upayunakti sā
english: But the sixteenth digit is subtle — let that be understood as the moon; it is not consumed by the gods, rather it is that which sustains the gods.

sanskrit: evaṃ tāṃ kṣapayitvā hi jāyate nṛpasattama sā hy asya prakṛtir dṛṣṭā tatkṣayān mokṣa ucyate
english: Thus, having wasted away that digit, he is born again, O best of kings; for this is seen to be his very nature, and from the wasting of it release is declared to come.

sanskrit: tad evaṃ ṣoḍaśakalaṃ deham avyaktasaṃjñakam mamāyam iti manvānas tatraiva parivartate
english: So, taking this sixteen-digit body, which bears the name of the Unmanifest, to be "mine," he keeps revolving within that very round.

sanskrit: pañcaviṃśas tathaivātmā tasyaivā pratibodhanāt vimalasya viśuddhasya śuddhānilaniṣevaṇāt
english: So too the twenty-fifth principle, the Self — through its failure to awaken, though it is stainless and wholly pure and frequents the pure breath of liberation —

sanskrit: aśuddha eva śuddhātmā tādṛg bhavati pārthiva abuddhasevanāc cāpi buddho 'py abudhatāṃ vrajet
english: the pure Self becomes as if impure, O lord of earth; and even one awakened, by keeping company with the unawakened, may sink back into unawakening.

sanskrit: tathaivāpratibuddho 'pi jñeyo nṛpatisattama prakṛtes triguṇāyās tu sevanāt prākṛto bhavet
english: In that very way the unawakened one is to be understood, O best of kings; through resorting to threefold-strained Nature he becomes a creature of Nature.

sanskrit: karālajanaka uvāca akṣarakṣarayor eṣa dvayoḥ saṃbandha iṣyate strīpuṃsor vāpi bhagavan saṃbandhas tadvad ucyate
english: Karāla-Janaka said: This union of the two, the Imperishable and the perishable, is held to exist; and the union of woman and man too, O blessed one, is said to be of just that kind.

sanskrit: ṛte na puruṣeṇeha strī garbhaṃ dhārayaty uta ṛte striyaṃ na puruṣo rūpaṃ nirvartayet tathā
english: Without the man no woman here conceives a child, and without the woman no man can bring a form into being.

sanskrit: anyonyasyābhisaṃbandhād anyonyaguṇasaṃśrayāt rūpaṃ nirvartayaty etad evaṃ sarvāsu yoniṣu
english: By their mutual union, by their resting one upon the other's qualities, form is brought forth — and so it is in all the wombs.

sanskrit: ratyartham abhisaṃrodhād anyonyaguṇasaṃśrayāt ṛtau nirvartate rūpaṃ tad vakṣyāmi nidarśanam
english: Through the union sought for pleasure, by their resting on one another's qualities, in due season form is brought forth — and I shall set out the proof of this.

sanskrit: ye guṇāḥ puruṣasyeha ye ca mātṛguṇās tathā asthi snāyu ca majjā ca jānīmaḥ pitṛto dvija
english: What qualities are the man's here, and what the mother's qualities — bone, sinew, and marrow we know to come from the father, O brāhmaṇa,

sanskrit: tvaṅ māṃsaṃ śoṇitaṃ caiva mātṛjāny api śuśruma evam etad dvijaśreṣṭha vedaśāstreṣu paṭhyate
english: while skin, flesh, and blood are mother-born — so we have heard; thus, O best of the twice-born, it is taught in the Vedas and the treatises.

sanskrit: pramāṇaṃ yac ca vedoktaṃ śāstroktaṃ yac ca paṭhyate vedaśāstrapramāṇaṃ ca pramāṇaṃ tat sanātanam
english: What the Veda declares is authority, and what the treatise declares and is recited; and the authority of Veda and treatise is the eternal standard.

sanskrit: evam evābhisaṃbaddhau nityaṃ prakṛtipūruṣau paśyāmi bhagavaṃs tasmān mokṣadharmo na vidyate
english: Just so I see Nature and Spirit forever bound together, O blessed one; and therefore no path of release exists, it seems to me.

sanskrit: atha vānantarakṛtaṃ kiṃ cid eva nidarśanam tan mamācakṣva tattvena pratyakṣo hy asi sarvathā
english: Or if there be some other proof drawn from a different ground, declare it to me truly, for you are in every way one of direct vision.

sanskrit: mokṣakāmā vayaṃ cāpi kāṅkṣāmo yad anāmayam adeham ajaraṃ divyam atīndriyam anīśvaram
english: We too long for release, and we yearn for that which is free of affliction — bodiless, ageless, divine, beyond the senses, owning no master.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca yad etad uktaṃ bhavatā vedaśāstranidarśanam evam etad yathā caitan na gṛhṇāti tathā bhavān
english: Vasiṣṭha said: This proof from Veda and treatise that you have stated is indeed so — but you have not grasped it as it truly is.

sanskrit: dhāryate hi tvayā grantha ubhayor vedaśāstrayoḥ na tu granthasya tattvajño yathāvat tvaṃ nareśvara
english: You hold the text of both the Veda and the treatise in your memory, O lord of men, but you do not know the truth of the text as it really is.

sanskrit: yo hi vede ca śāstre ca granthadhāraṇatatparaḥ na ca granthārthatattvajñas tasya tad dhāraṇaṃ vṛthā
english: For one bent on retaining the text in Veda and treatise, yet who does not know the truth of the text's meaning — his retaining of it is in vain.

sanskrit: bhāraṃ sa vahate tasya granthasyārthaṃ na vetti yaḥ yas tu granthārthatattvajño nāsya granthāgamo vṛthā
english: He merely carries a burden who does not know the meaning of the text; but for one who knows the truth of the text's meaning, his learning of the text is not in vain.

sanskrit: granthasyārthaṃ ca pṛṣṭaḥ saṃs tādṛśo vaktum arhati yathā tattvābhigamanād arthaṃ tasya sa vindati
english: Such a man, when asked the meaning of the text, is fit to declare it; for by approaching its truth he attains the meaning of that text.

sanskrit: yas tu saṃsatsu kathayed granthārthaṃ sthūlabuddhimān sa kathaṃ mandavijñāno granthaṃ vakṣyati nirṇayāt
english: But one of coarse understanding who would expound the text's meaning in assemblies — how, being dull of discernment, shall he expound the text with sure conclusion?

sanskrit: nirṇayaṃ cāpi chidrātmā na taṃ vakṣyati tattvataḥ sopahāsātmatām eti yasmāc caivātmavān api
english: A flawed mind cannot state the conclusion truly; and even a man of some self-command thereby falls into a state of ridicule.

sanskrit: tasmāt tvaṃ śṛṇu rājendra yathaitad anudṛśyate yāthātathyena sāṃkhyeṣu yogeṣu ca mahātmasu
english: Therefore listen, O lord of kings, to how this is rightly seen as it is, among the great souls who follow Sāṃkhya and Yoga.

sanskrit: yad eva yogāḥ paśyanti sāṃkhyais tad anugamyate ekaṃ sāṃkhyaṃ ca yogaṃ ca yaḥ paśyati sa buddhimān
english: What the followers of Yoga see is followed also by the Sāṃkhyas; and he who sees Sāṃkhya and Yoga as one — he is the man of true insight.

sanskrit: tvaṅ māṃsaṃ rudhiraṃ medaḥ pittaṃ majjāsthi snāyu ca etad aindriyakaṃ tāta yad bhavān idam āha vai
english: Skin, flesh, blood, fat, bile, marrow, bone, and sinew — all this belongs to the senses, dear one, this of which you have just spoken.

sanskrit: dravyād dravyasya niṣpattir indriyād indriyaṃ tathā dehād deham avāpnoti bījād bījaṃ tathaiva ca
english: From substance arises substance, and likewise sense from sense; one obtains body from body, and seed from seed in the same way.

sanskrit: nirindriyasyābījasya nirdravyasyāsya dehinaḥ kathaṃ guṇā bhaviṣyanti nirguṇatvān mahātmanaḥ
english: But for this embodied Self, which is without sense, without seed, without substance, how shall there be qualities, since the great Self is free of qualities?

sanskrit: guṇā guṇeṣu jāyante tatraiva niviśanti ca evaṃ guṇāḥ prakṛtito jāyante ca na santi ca
english: Qualities arise within qualities and there too they subside; thus qualities are born of Nature, and yet in themselves they have no being.

sanskrit: tvaṅ māṃsaṃ rudhiraṃ medaḥ pittaṃ majjāsthi snāyu ca aṣṭau tāny atha śukreṇa jānīhi prākṛtāni vai
english: Skin, flesh, blood, fat, bile, marrow, bone, and sinew — know these eight, together with semen, to be of Nature indeed.

sanskrit: pumāṃś caivāpumāṃś caiva trailiṅgyaṃ prākṛtaṃ smṛtam naiva pumān pumāṃś caiva sa liṅgīty abhidhīyate
english: Male and not-male and the threefold-marked — this is held to belong to Nature; he who is neither truly male nor not male is called the one possessed of marks.

sanskrit: aliṅgā prakṛtir liṅgair upalabhyati sātmajaiḥ yathā puṣpaphalair nityam ṛtavo mūrtayas tathā
english: Nature, herself without mark, is apprehended through the marks born of her, just as the seasons are ever made manifest in form by their flowers and fruits.

sanskrit: evam apy anumānena hy aliṅgam upalabhyate pañcaviṃśatimas tāta liṅgeṣv aniyatātmakaḥ
english: In the same way, even the markless is apprehended through inference; the twenty-fifth, dear one, is of unbound nature amid the marks.

sanskrit: anādinidhano 'nantaḥ sarvadarśī nirāmayaḥ kevalaṃ tv abhimānitvād guṇeṣv aguṇa ucyate
english: Without beginning or end, infinite, all-seeing, free of affliction — yet merely through self-conceit it is called, amid the qualities, the qualityless one.

sanskrit: guṇā guṇavataḥ santi nirguṇasya kuto guṇāḥ tasmād evaṃ vijānanti ye janā guṇadarśinaḥ
english: Qualities belong to one possessed of qualities; whence should there be qualities for the qualityless? Thus do those people understand it who discern the qualities.

sanskrit: yadā tv eṣa guṇān sarvān prākṛtān abhimanyate tadā sa guṇavān eva parameṇānupaśyati
english: But when this Self conceives all the qualities of Nature as its own, then it appears as one possessed of qualities — though by the highest view it is otherwise.

sanskrit: yat tad buddheḥ paraṃ prāhuḥ sāṃkhyā yogāś ca sarvaśaḥ budhyamānaṃ mahāprājñam abuddhaparivarjanāt
english: That which the Sāṃkhyas and the Yogins everywhere declare to be beyond the intellect — the awakening, the supremely wise — comes through the forsaking of the unawakened state.

sanskrit: aprabuddham athāvyaktaṃ saguṇaṃ prāhur īśvaram nirguṇaṃ ceśvaraṃ nityam adhiṣṭhātāram eva ca
english: The unawakened Unmanifest, endowed with qualities, they call the Lord; and the qualityless Lord too, eternal and the abiding overseer.

sanskrit: prakṛteś ca guṇānāṃ ca pañcaviṃśatikaṃ budhāḥ sāṃkhyayoge ca kuśalā budhyante paramaiṣiṇaḥ
english: The twenty-fifth, beyond Nature and the qualities, the wise ones understand — they who are skilled in Sāṃkhya and Yoga and who seek the highest.

sanskrit: yadā prabuddhās tv avyaktam avasthājanmabhīravaḥ budhyamānaṃ prabudhyanti gamayanti samaṃ tadā
english: When the awakened ones, fearful of the births that come with worldly states, fully comprehend the awakening one beyond the Unmanifest, then they bring it to that selfsame oneness.

sanskrit: etan nidarśanaṃ samyag asamyag anudarśanam budhyamānāprabuddhābhyāṃ pṛthak pṛthag ariṃdama
english: This is the right discernment and that the wrong discernment, drawn severally from the awakening one and the unawakened, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: paraspareṇaitad uktaṃ kṣarākṣaranidarśanam ekatvam akṣaraṃ prāhur nānātvaṃ kṣaram ucyate
english: Thus, set one against the other, is told the proof of the perishable and the Imperishable: oneness they call the Imperishable, and manifoldness is called the perishable.

sanskrit: pañcaviṃśatiniṣṭho 'yaṃ yadāsamyak pravartate ekatvaṃ darśanaṃ cāsya nānātvaṃ cāpy adarśanam
english: When this one, grounded in the twenty-fifth, proceeds wrongly, then his vision is of oneness, and yet there is also a failure to see, in manifoldness.

sanskrit: tattvanistattvayor etat pṛthag eva nidarśanam pañcaviṃśatisargaṃ tu tattvam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: This is the distinct proof of the principled and the unprincipled; but the creation that ends in the twenty-fifth the wise call the principled.

sanskrit: nistattvaṃ pañcaviṃśasya param āhur nidarśanam vargasya vargam ācāraṃ tattvaṃ tattvāt sanātanam
english: That which is beyond the twenty-fifth they call the proof of the unprincipled; class upon class, and discipline, and principle beyond principle — eternal.

sanskrit: karālajanaka uvāca nānātvaikatvam ity uktaṃ tvayaitad ṛṣisattama paśyāmi cābhisaṃdigdham etayor vai nidarśanam
english: Karāla-Janaka said: Manifoldness and oneness — this you have declared, O best of seers; yet I see the proof of these two as still beset with doubt.

sanskrit: tathāprabuddhabuddhābhyāṃ budhyamānasya cānagha sthūlabuddhyā na paśyāmi tattvam etan na saṃśayaḥ
english: So too of the unawakened and the awakened and of the awakening one, O sinless one, with my coarse understanding I do not see the truth of this — there is no doubt.

sanskrit: akṣarakṣarayor uktaṃ tvayā yad api kāraṇam tad apy asthirabuddhitvāt pranaṣṭam iva me 'nagha
english: And the cause you declared concerning the Imperishable and the perishable — that too, through my unsteady understanding, has all but slipped away from me, O sinless one.

sanskrit: tad etac chrotum icchāmi nānātvaikatvadarśanam buddham apratibuddhaṃ ca budhyamānaṃ ca tattvataḥ
english: This I wish to hear: the vision of manifoldness and oneness, and the awakened, the unawakened, and the awakening one, in their truth.

sanskrit: vidyāvidye ca bhagavann akṣaraṃ kṣaram eva ca sāṃkhyaṃ yogaṃ ca kārtsnyena pṛthak caivāpṛthak ca ha
english: And knowledge and ignorance, O blessed one, the Imperishable and the perishable, and Sāṃkhya and Yoga in their fullness — both severally and together.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca hanta te saṃpravakṣyāmi yad etad anupṛcchasi yogakṛtyaṃ mahārāja pṛthag eva śṛṇuṣva me
english: Vasiṣṭha said: Come then, I shall set forth for you that which you ask — the practice of Yoga, O great king; hear it from me first, by itself.

sanskrit: yogakṛtyaṃ tu yogānāṃ dhyānam eva paraṃ balam tac cāpi dvividhaṃ dhyānam āhur vedavido janāḥ
english: The chief practice of the followers of Yoga is meditation, their supreme strength; and that meditation, those versed in the Veda declare to be of two kinds.

sanskrit: ekāgratā ca manasaḥ prāṇāyāmas tathaiva ca prāṇāyāmas tu saguṇo nirguṇo manasas tathā
english: Single-pointedness of mind, and likewise the restraint of breath: the restraint of breath belongs to the qualified, while the stilling of the mind belongs to the unqualified.

sanskrit: mūtrotsarge purīṣe ca bhojane ca narādhipa trikālaṃ nābhiyuñjīta śeṣaṃ yuñjīta tatparaḥ
english: In passing water, in voiding the bowels, and in eating, O ruler of men — at these three times let him not yoke himself; the rest of the time, intent, let him practice the yoga.

sanskrit: indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyo nivartya manasā muniḥ daśadvādaśabhir vāpi caturviṃśāt paraṃ tataḥ
english: Withdrawing the senses from the objects of sense by the mind, the sage — by tens or by twelves, and then beyond the twenty-fourth —

sanskrit: taṃ codanābhir matimān ātmānaṃ codayed atha tiṣṭhantam ajaraṃ taṃ tu yat tad uktaṃ manīṣibhiḥ
english: with urgings the wise man should urge on that Self, the ageless one abiding there, of which the thoughtful have spoken.

sanskrit: taiś cātmā satataṃ jñeya ity evam anuśuśruma dravyaṃ hy ahīnamanaso nānyatheti viniścayaḥ
english: And by these the Self is ever to be known — so we have heard in succession; it is a thing graspable only by one whose mind is undiminished, and not otherwise — this is the settled truth.

sanskrit: vimuktaḥ sarvasaṅgebhyo laghvāhāro jitendriyaḥ pūrvarātre pare caiva dhārayeta mano ''tmani
english: Freed from all attachments, light in his eating, his senses conquered, in the first watch of the night and in the last let him fix the mind upon the Self.

sanskrit: sthirīkṛtyendriyagrāmaṃ manasā mithileśvara mano buddhyā sthiraṃ kṛtvā pāṣāṇa iva niścalaḥ
english: Having steadied the host of the senses by the mind, O lord of Mithilā, and having made the mind firm by the intellect, let him be unmoving like a stone,

sanskrit: sthāṇuvac cāpy akampaḥ syād girivac cāpi niścalaḥ budhā vidhividhānajñās tadā yuktaṃ pracakṣate
english: unshaken as a post, immovable as a mountain; then the wise, who know the ordinances of the rule, declare him to be yoked.

sanskrit: na śṛṇoti na cāghrāti na rasyati na paśyati na ca sparśaṃ vijānāti na saṃkalpayate manaḥ
english: He hears not, nor smells, nor tastes, nor sees, nor is aware of touch, nor does the mind form any intention;

sanskrit: na cābhimanyate kiṃ cin na ca budhyati kāṣṭhavat tadā prakṛtim āpannaṃ yuktam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: he conceives nothing, nor is he aware of aught, like a log of wood — then the thoughtful call him yoked, returned to his own Nature.

sanskrit: nivāte ca yathā dīpyan dīpas tadvat sa dṛśyate niriṅgaś cācalaś cordhvaṃ na tiryaggatim āpnuyāt
english: As a lamp burning in a windless place — so is he seen: steady and unmoving, rising upward, taking no sideways course.

sanskrit: tadā tam anupaśyeta yasmin dṛṣṭe tu kathyate hṛdayastho 'ntarātmeti jñeyo jñas tāta madvidhaiḥ
english: Then let him behold that Self, on whose being seen it is said — "the inner Self that dwells in the heart" — the Knower to be known, dear one, by such as I am.

sanskrit: vidhūma iva saptārcir āditya iva raśmimān vaidyuto 'gnir ivākāśe dṛśyate ''tmā tathātmani
english: Like the seven-tongued fire without smoke, like the sun bright with rays, like the fire of lightning in the sky — so is the Self seen within the self.

sanskrit: yaṃ paśyanti mahātmāno dhṛtimanto manīṣiṇaḥ brāhmaṇā brahmayoniṣṭhā hy ayonim amṛtātmakam
english: Whom the great souls behold, the steadfast and the thoughtful, the brāhmaṇas grounded in the womb of Brahman — the wombless one, immortal in essence.

sanskrit: tad evāhur aṇubhyo 'ṇu tan mahadbhyo mahattaram tadantaḥ sarvabhūteṣu dhruvaṃ tiṣṭhan na dṛśyate
english: That very one they call subtler than the subtle, greater than the great; it abides within, fixed in all beings, yet is not seen.

sanskrit: buddhidravyeṇa dṛśyeta manodīpena lokakṛt mahatas tamasas tāta pāre tiṣṭhann atāmasaḥ
english: By the instrument of the intellect, by the lamp of the mind, the maker of the world may be seen — dwelling beyond the great darkness, dear one, himself untouched by darkness.

sanskrit: sa tamonuda ity uktas tattvajñair vedapāragaiḥ vimalo vitamaskaś ca nirliṅgo 'liṅgasaṃjñitaḥ
english: He is called the dispeller of darkness by those who know the truth and have crossed to the far shore of the Veda — stainless, free of gloom, without mark, known by the name of the markless.

sanskrit: yogam etad dhi yogānāṃ manye yogasya lakṣaṇam evaṃ paśyaṃ prapaśyanti ātmānam ajaraṃ param
english: This indeed I deem the Yoga of those who practice Yoga, the very mark of Yoga; seeing thus, they behold the Self, the ageless and supreme.

sanskrit: yogadarśanam etāvad uktaṃ te tattvato mayā sāṃkhyajñānaṃ pravakṣyāmi parisaṃkhyānidarśanam
english: Thus far have I declared to you, in truth, the vision of Yoga; now I shall set forth the knowledge of Sāṃkhya, the proof by full enumeration.
